title: Enable-gated EX/MEM stall hold
motivation:
The EX/MEM register is on the placed baseline's critical ID/EX-to-EX/MEM path.
Its current dmem-stall branch explicitly feeds every field back to itself,

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite the EX/MEM hold as an enable-style sequential update: reset still
clears the register, and every non-stalled priority case writes exactly the
same payload, but a dmem stall performs no assignment. This preserves the
pipeline's hold/retirement semantics while allowing Yosys to infer DFFRE
cells and remove the stall-select mux from the hot EX result path. The change
is deliberately limited to the existing register boundary, not forwarding,
control flow, memory ordering, or RVFI behavior.

title: Registered PC-relative target path
motivation:
The execute stage calculates PC-relative targets for every instruction and
carries branch-only metadata through EX/MEM even though later stages never
consume it. After the divider and memory-path improvements, that unnecessary
add-and-fanout cone is a plausible remaining Fmax limiter.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Partition PC-relative target generation at the registered ID/EX boundary:
decode computes and registers the branch/JAL PC-plus-immediate target, while

combinational target net. This keeps speculation and retirement unchanged,
but shortens the common EX control cone without recreating the earlier
fetch-feedback or high-fanout shared-adder designs.

title: Decode-confirmed branch target cache
motivation:
CoreMark repeatedly executes a small set of conditional loop branches, but every
prior fetch-stage predictor degraded Fmax by adding lookup or decode to the
PC feedback path. The current EX redirect also discards two younger instructions
on each taken iteration.

prior fetch-stage predictor degraded Fmax by adding lookup or decode to the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a tiny direct-mapped branch target cache that is trained only by resolved,
valid conditional branches in EX, but consume it in decode only after the
fetched instruction has been validated as a legal BRANCH. A matching trained
entry supplies a registered target and one-bit taken state, so decode can
redirect a predicted-taken loop one stage earlier without placing lookup logic
on the normal IF PC+4 feedback path or allowing an alias to redirect a
non-branch under symbolic instruction memory. Carry a predicted-successor bit
only with the accepted branch; EX compares and recovers only for that predicted
branch, while non-predicted instructions retain the existing EX redirect path.
This removes one loop-back bubble after warm-up and limits new recovery logic
to the relatively rare predicted-control path rather than every EX instruction.
